tip: For know-how, 'could cook' uses 'saber', not 'poder': 'se eu soubesse cozinhar' is 'if I could cook'.
Here 'quem' means whoever or those who, and it takes a singular verb, so 'estuda' and 'passa'.
'Tudo que' is a set phrase for everything that; Brazilians usually drop the 'o' of 'tudo o que'.
'Ter' plus a participle, 'tenho corrido', means an action repeated up to now, not one finished event like the English present perfect.
'Come-se bem' means 'one eats well'; the 'se' leaves the verb with no named subject, like English 'one' or 'you'.
'Gostar' always needs 'de' before its object, so it is 'gosto de pessoas', never 'gosto pessoas'.
Here 'como' means the way in which, linking back to 'a forma': 'a forma como ele fala' is the way he talks.
'Assistir' meaning to watch formally takes 'a' before its object, but Brazilians often drop it, as in 'a série que estou assistindo'.
'A gente' means we but takes a singular verb, so it is 'a gente tem se comunicado', never 'têm'.
After a time word like 'o dia', Portuguese uses 'em que', not 'quando': 'o dia em que nos conhecemos' is the day we met.
'Como se', meaning as if, takes the imperfect subjunctive, giving 'soubesse' rather than plain 'sabia'.
For a hypothetical, 'se' plus the imperfect subjunctive 'tivesse' pairs with the conditional 'ensinaria'.
For where a place is located, 'ficar' is the natural verb, so 'fica no centro' means it sits downtown.
The object pronoun 'o' here means him and sits before the verb: 'o contratou' means hired him.
'Cobrir' has the irregular participle 'coberto', not 'cobrido', as in 'tinha coberto o bolo'.
'Quem dera' expresses a wish, if only, and is followed by the imperfect subjunctive 'pudesse'.
After a preposition, Portuguese often uses 'o qual', so 'trabalhar em' gives 'o projeto no qual estamos trabalhando'.
'Pagar' has two participles: with 'ter' the standard pick is 'pagado', as in 'tínhamos pagado', while 'pago' goes with 'ser' or 'estar'.
'Procurar' means look for and takes a direct object, so 'procurado emprego', with no preposition after it.
An impersonal opinion like 'era importante que' forces the subjunctive, so 'soubessem', not 'sabiam'.
'Todo mundo' means everyone but takes a singular verb, as in 'todo mundo sabe', never 'todo mundo sabem'.
Here 'caça com gato', 'hunts with a cat', is part of a saying: you make do with what you have.
Adding '-se' to a verb hides the doer: 'vende-se apartamento' = apartment for sale, no seller named.
The present perfect with 'tem', as in 'tem praticado', means an ongoing or repeated action up to now, not one finished event.
'Formar-se' means to graduate; the 'se' sits between 'tinha' and 'formado': 'tinha se formado'.
'Sem que' (without) always triggers the subjunctive: 'sem que ninguém percebesse', never 'percebeu'.
'Ver' has the irregular participle 'visto', not 'vido': 'tinham visto esse filme' = had seen this movie.
'Assistir' meaning to watch formally needs the preposition 'a': 'assistido a esse episódio', not 'assistido esse'.
'Pensar' pairs with 'em' for think about: 'tenho pensado em mudar de carreira', where 'em' marks the topic.
'A gente' means we but takes a singular verb: 'a gente tem se visto', never 'a gente temos'.
